data.title: First Western signals 1% ROA during 2027 as loan growth outlook points to mid-teens pace
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: First Western Financial (MYFW) Q3 2026

Management view

  • "We executed well in the third quarter and saw positive trends in many areas, including loan growth, improving deposit mix, net interest margin expansion, trust and investment management fee growth, well-managed expenses, and improved asset quality." (Founder, Chairman, CEO & President Scott Wylie)
  • "Pre-tax, pre-provision net income increased 15% in the third quarter, that's not annualized, compared to the prior quarter, and 27% compared to the third quarter 2025." (CEO Wylie)
  • "We generated net income of about $6 million, or $0.60 per diluted share, in the third quarter" and "our tangible book value per share increased by 3% this quarter to $26.28." (CEO Wylie)
  • "Our loans held for investment increased $95 million from the end of the prior quarter, marking the sixth consecutive quarterly increase" and "new loan production was $163 million in the third quarter." (COO & Director Julie Courkamp)
  • "Our total deposits increased 2.5% from the end of the prior quarter with growth in non-interest bearing and money market accounts" and "average non-interest bearing deposits increased $14 million or 3.9% in the quarter." (COO Courkamp)
  • "Our NIM increased 5 basis points from the prior quarter to 2.95%." (Principal Accounting Officer, CFO & Treasurer David Weber)

Outlook

  • "Based on our third quarter performance and what we're seeing in our markets, we're encouraged and we expect further improvement in our financial performance in the fourth quarter of the year." (CEO Wylie)
  • "Our loan pipeline remains strong and should fuel solid loan growth going forward" and "we expect positive trends to continue across several key areas, including loan growth, deposit growth, deposit mix improvement, net interest margin expansion, and increased activity in our wealth management business." (CEO Wylie)
  • "We're seeing good opportunities to add new clients and banking talent due to the ongoing disruption from M&A activity in our markets." (CEO Wylie)
  • Change vs. prior quarter guidance language: Q3 emphasized momentum and continuation, including "We had a net interest margin expansion of 26 basis points in 2025 and another 24 basis points in expansion so far in 2026. This will continue." (CEO Wylie) compared with Q2’s "another 19 basis points so far in 2026" and expectation of improvement "in the second half of the year." (CEO Wylie, Q2)

Financial results

  • "Our gross revenue increased 2.8% from the prior quarter, primarily due to an increase in net interest income partially offset by a decrease in non-interest income." (CFO Weber)
  • "Our net interest income increased 5.5% from the prior quarter" and "our net interest income increased 18% from the third quarter of 2025." (CFO Weber)
  • "Our non-interest income decreased by $600,000 from the prior quarter" driven by "a decrease in net gain on sale of mortgage loans" and "a decrease in bank fees, partially offset by an increase in trust and investment management fees." (CFO Weber)
  • "Our non-interest expense decreased $400,000 from the prior quarter" including that Q2 had "a $400,000 non-recurring charge that we recorded in the second quarter of '26." (CFO Weber)
  • "Our non-performing asset ratio decreased to 39 basis points in the third quarter" and "increased loan volume contributed to a provision of $600,000 during the third quarter of 2026." (CFO Weber)

Q&A

  • Hannah Wynn, KBW: asked whether Q3’s "14% number" loan growth can repeat and how pipelines look into 2027; CEO Wylie: "pipelines are stronger and continue to be strong" and "our forecast for this year, kind of, 10%-ish growth, seems like we're on track for that, and I think a 15% run rate here going into... 2027... seems like a reasonable indication of what we're seeing." (CEO Wylie)
  • Hannah Wynn, KBW: asked about mortgage activity if rates rise; CEO Wylie: "mortgages as a percent of revenues for us is a small number" and management highlighted wealth fees momentum: "our trust and investment management fees were up over $100,000 in Q3" and "those are trends that we haven't seen in years here." (CEO Wylie)
  • Matthew Clark, Piper Sandler: asked for spot deposit rate and betas; CFO Weber: "the spot deposit rate for total deposits was 2.86% at the end of September" and "we saw a 28% beta on that September hike" on standard money markets, while index money markets "would translate to 100% beta." (CFO Weber)
  • Matthew Clark, Piper Sandler: asked about quarter-end borrowings and NIM implications; CFO Weber: "on an average basis, we do expect that to normalize." (CFO Weber)
  • Matthew Clark, Piper Sandler: asked timing to reach 1% ROA; CEO Wylie: "we do think that we'll be operating a 1% ROA during 2027" and added, "we can see a line of sight to... 1.5% ROA" under specified macro conditions. (CEO Wylie)
  • Liam Coohill, Hovde: asked what’s driving noninterest-bearing growth; CEO Wylie: "a big driver... is all of this market disruption" and disclosed a leadership hire: "we added Bill Sullivan as our Head of Strategic Planning here." (CEO Wylie)
  • Liam Coohill, Hovde: asked about higher payoffs and rate mix; CFO Weber: "the payoff number seems to be about $100 million a quarter" and "there's no big trend." (CFO Weber)
  • Liam Coohill, Hovde: asked about tax rate normalization; CFO Weber: "it was a one-time in the quarter" and "the 23% effective tax rate is a reasonable... estimate." (CFO Weber)
  • William Dezellem, Tieton: asked about an accelerating "flywheel" and potential 20% loan growth; CEO Wylie: "those green shoots seem to be sprouting a little bit more" but "mid-teen growth is a great place to be" and "don't need to do" 20%-25% growth if it reduces selectivity. (CEO Wylie)
  • William Dezellem, Tieton: asked about note redemption; CFO Weber: the company called "a $10 million note" that was "eligible for call" and said it "will give us a benefit from a NIM perspective." (CFO Weber)

Sentiment analysis

  • Analysts tone was slightly positive, with supportive phrasing such as "it was great to see" (Hannah Wynn, KBW) and "Nice quarter" (Ross Haberman, RLH Investments in Q2), while focusing questions on sustainability of loan growth, deposit betas, borrowings, and profitability targets.
  • Management tone was positive and confident in prepared remarks, using language such as "we're encouraged" and "This will continue." (CEO Wylie), and in Q&A leaned confident but cautious on precision: "I'm always reluctant to say... this percent" while still providing directional targets like "10%-ish growth" and "15% run rate... into 2027." (CEO Wylie)
  • Versus Q2, Q3 confidence language tightened around continuation and acceleration ("pipelines are stronger"; "green shoots... sprouting"), while Q2 included more balancing language around pricing discipline and the NIM-versus-growth trade-off. (CEO Wylie, Q2 and Q3)

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • Q3 shifted emphasis from Q2’s discussion of balancing growth vs. NIM to executing on both, highlighting "loan growth" and "net interest margin expansion" in the same opening summary. (CEO Wylie, Q3) Q2 had framed a potential trade-off: "be a little bit more flexible on NIM improvement to try and drive better growth." (CEO Wylie, Q2)
  • Q3 highlighted stronger balance sheet momentum, including "loans held for investment increased $95 million" versus Q2’s "$23 million" increase, alongside higher quarterly "new loan production" of "$163 million" versus "$115 million" in Q2. (COO Courkamp, Q3 and Q2)
  • Q3 introduced a new senior hire and broader recruiting narrative ("Bill Sullivan as our Head of Strategic Planning" and "14 hires now we've made of senior folks out of what used to be FirstBank"), while Q2 referenced "new leadership in Arizona" without naming the individual. (CEO Wylie, Q3 and Q2)

Risks and concerns

  • "Origination volumes were negatively impacted by higher mortgage rates" in mortgage banking, with management positioning the business as "strategically important" but "a small number" in revenue mix. (CFO Weber; CEO Wylie)
  • Deposit pricing sensitivity remained a focal risk in Q&A, with management disclosing rate mechanics and hedging: "we do have $200 million notional of capital cash flow hedge on the deposit portfolio." (CFO Weber)
  • Competitive behavior in loan pricing was flagged as a market risk: management described competitors pricing "at 90% and 95%... basis points over comparable treasuries" and reiterated selectivity. (CEO Wylie)

Final takeaway

Management described Q3 as a quarter where improving loan growth, a better deposit mix, and net interest margin expansion coincided with tighter expense control and improved asset quality, while also pointing to early traction from a reorganized planning, trust, and investment management effort. Leadership framed market disruption from M&A as a recruiting and client acquisition catalyst, outlined a directional view of "10%-ish" loan growth for 2026 and a "15% run rate" into 2027, and stated an expectation to be "operating a 1% ROA during 2027," while acknowledging that quarterly growth can "bounce around" and that mortgage-related fee income remains pressured by higher rates.

data.title: First Hawaiian outlines 1%-2% full-year loan growth as it expects Q4 NIM of 3.34%-3.35%
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: First Hawaiian (FHB) Q3 2026

Management view

  • "I'll start by providing an update on the acquisition. ... we're making good progress obtaining the necessary regulatory and shareholder approvals... Integration planning is going well, and we continue to expect to close this quarter." (Chairman of the Board, President & CEO Robert Harrison)
  • "Net interest income increased, deposit costs declined, while deposit balances grew, and the margin increased 5 basis points." (Chairman of the Board, President & CEO Robert Harrison)
  • "The $24.3 million tax settlement expense stemmed from a settlement with the State of California on tax liabilities resulting from our 2016 separation from BNP Paribas." (Chairman of the Board, President & CEO Robert Harrison)
  • "Total loans declined $115 million in the quarter. Decline was primarily due to unexpected CRE loan payoffs, a slight decline in dealer floor plan balances and runoff in the residential loan portfolio." (Chairman of the Board, President & CEO Robert Harrison)
  • "Net interest income was $174.1 million, $3.1 million more than the prior quarter... The NIM in the third quarter was 3.30%, up 5 basis points linked quarter." (Vice Chairman of Finance Group & CFO James Moses)
  • "Noninterest expense in the third quarter was $160 million. The quarter included $6.7 million of merger-related costs... [and] a $24.3 million expense related to a California tax settlement agreement." (Vice Chairman of Finance Group & CFO James Moses)
  • "Third quarter net charge-offs were $21.9 million or 60 basis points of total loans and leases... primarily driven by a $12.5 million partial charge-off... on an office building located in downtown Seattle." (Executive VP & Chief Risk Officer Lea Nakamura)

Outlook

  • "We're reducing our full year loan outlook to 1% to 2% growth, down from 3% to 4% growth." (Chairman of the Board, President & CEO Robert Harrison)
  • "We expect NIM in the fourth quarter to be between 3.34% to 3.35%, which increases our full year NIM outlook to 3.26% to 3.27%." (Chairman of the Board, President & CEO Robert Harrison)
  • "Our outlook for noninterest income remains about $220 million for the full year." (Chairman of the Board, President & CEO Robert Harrison)
  • "Our full year outlook is now in the $510 million to $515 million range" for expenses excluding merger-related costs and the Q3 tax settlement expense, and "we're expecting approximately $25 million in merger-related costs in the fourth quarter." (Chairman of the Board, President & CEO Robert Harrison)

Financial results

  • "Net interest income was $174.1 million" and "noninterest income was $56.1 million." (Vice Chairman of Finance Group & CFO James Moses)
  • "Total deposits were up about $50 million, while our total cost of deposits fell by 3 basis points" and "our noninterest-bearing deposit ratio was 32%." (Vice Chairman of Finance Group & CFO James Moses)
  • "The NIM in the third quarter was 3.30%" and "noninterest expense in the third quarter was $160 million." (Vice Chairman of Finance Group & CFO James Moses)
  • "The allowance for credit losses decreased by $4 million to $164 million with a coverage ratio of 1.14% of total loans and leases." (Executive VP & Chief Risk Officer Lea Nakamura)

Q&A

  • Andrew Terrell, Stephens: Asked about Q4 loan growth and pipelines; Chairman of the Board, President & CEO Harrison said "the pipeline is still there" but highlighted "the continuing battle of things getting paid off" and "things that are unexpected."
  • Andrew Terrell, Stephens: Asked about post-TriCo margin expectations; Vice Chairman of Finance Group & CFO Moses said "That's kind of hard for me to answer at the moment," and pointed to "about $400 million or so a quarter" of fixed-rate cash flow repricing and a spread "maybe 160 to 170 kind of going forward."
  • David Feaster, Raymond James: Asked if funding costs have more room to fall; Vice Chairman of Finance Group & CFO Moses said "I think we're kind of at a trough in this quarter" and described competitive pressures in Hawaii as "muted."
  • David Feaster, Raymond James: Pressed on integration execution risk; Chairman of the Board, President & CEO Harrison said "we're very focused on that" and "the vast majority are staying on with us" while emphasizing "The execution risk is what we're completely focused on."
  • Anthony Elian, JPMorgan: Asked about commercial deposit growth and credit reviews; Vice Chairman of Finance Group & CFO Moses described commercial deposit change as "sort of normal flows," while Executive VP & Chief Risk Officer Nakamura said "We've been watching very carefully" and "We don't have very much in Mainland office."
  • Matthew Clark, Piper Sandler: Asked for spot rates, repricing mix, and SNC detail; Vice Chairman of Finance Group & CFO Moses said deposit spot rate "was 117 basis points" and September spot NIM "was 3.33%," and Executive VP & Chief Risk Officer Nakamura said C&I SNC was "$275 million in outstanding" with "an $11.6 million unfunded commitment" rated special mention; management said on CRE SNCs "We might have to get back to you." (Chairman of the Board, President & CEO Harrison)
  • Andrew Liesch, StoneX: Asked about buybacks post-close and Basel III; Chairman of the Board, President & CEO Harrison said buybacks are "on the table" but "a little bit early to decide how much and when," and Vice Chairman of Finance Group & CFO Moses said Basel III impact was expected to be "maybe 100 basis points to CET1."

Sentiment analysis

  • Analysts tone was slightly negative to neutral, with repeated probing on the loan-growth reset, credit “one-off” framing, and integration execution risk, including questions that stressed "one of the bigger risks with the deal" (David Feaster, Raymond James).
  • Management tone was neutral to slightly positive in prepared remarks, but more cautious in Q&A on uncertainties, including "That's kind of hard for me to answer" on pro forma margin (Vice Chairman of Finance Group & CFO Moses) and "It's really... unexpected" payoffs affecting loan growth (Chairman of the Board, President & CEO Harrison).
  • Versus the prior quarter, language shifted from Q2 confidence in "full year loan growth... 3% to 4%" to Q3’s explicit cut to "1% to 2% growth" (Chairman of the Board, President & CEO Harrison), with Q&A spending more time on credit noise and integration mechanics.

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • Loan narrative flipped from Q2 "Total loans grew $137 million" (Chairman of the Board, President & CEO Robert Harrison) to Q3 "Total loans declined $115 million" driven by "unexpected CRE loan payoffs" (Chairman of the Board, President & CEO Harrison), prompting a guidance reduction.
  • Credit discussion intensified: Q2 emphasized "strong credit performance and healthy credit metrics" (Executive VP & Chief Risk Officer Lea Nakamura), while Q3 featured "$21.9 million" net charge-offs and downgrades tied to office and CRE reviews (Executive VP & Chief Risk Officer Nakamura).
  • Deal commentary progressed from Q2 "recently announced deal" with "no new information" beyond prior materials (Chairman of the Board, President & CEO Harrison) to Q3 detailing approval milestones and staff retention, including "shareholder special meetings on October 29" and an expectation "to close this quarter" (Chairman of the Board, President & CEO Harrison).

Risks and concerns

  • "Unexpected CRE loan payoffs" were cited as a key swing factor for loan growth. (Chairman of the Board, President & CEO Robert Harrison)
  • Credit risk centered on the Seattle office participation and rate pressure on legacy-originations: "This loan... has struggled due to... contraction in office demand and higher-for-longer interest rates." (Executive VP & Chief Risk Officer Lea Nakamura)
  • Operational risk was flagged in mortgage servicing: elevated past due/nonperforming metrics were "primarily related to operational issues arising out of the recent outsourcing of our residential mortgage servicing." (Executive VP & Chief Risk Officer Lea Nakamura)
  • Integration risk remained a major focus, with management emphasizing execution: "The execution risk is what we're completely focused on." (Chairman of the Board, President & CEO Robert Harrison)

Final takeaway

Management framed Q3 as solid core performance with higher NIM and lower deposit costs, but reset the full-year loan growth outlook to 1%-2% after unexpected CRE payoffs and discussed credit “noise” driven by a $12.5 million partial charge-off on a Seattle office participation and several CRE downgrades. Leadership also reiterated that TriCo remains on track to close in Q4, highlighted active integration planning and retention efforts, and guided to a higher full-year NIM range while flagging approximately $25 million of Q4 merger-related costs.

data.title: Hess Midstream upgraded at Raymond James as Chevron restructuring selloff overdone
data.description:
Hess Midstream (HESM) rose 2.2% in Friday's trading as Raymond James raised its rating to Market Outperform from Market Perform with a $32 price target, saying its recent selloff following the Chevron (CVX) restructuring has created an attractive entry point for investors.

The Bakken contract reset was severe, reducing estimated 2027 EBITDA by $400M while pausing distribution growth and increasing leverage, yet Chevron's (CVX) ~38% ownership cancellation, contribution of D-J Basin assets, and contract extensions to 2045 provide Hess Midstream (HESM) with a meaningful exchange of value for the lower rates, Raymond James analyst J.R. Weston said.

The pause in 2027 distribution growth has weighted on Hess Midstream (HESM) sentiment, but the payout looks supported by $525M-$625M of guided adjusted free cash flow against $420M-$425M of distribution, which Weston said should allow leverage to move from 3.75x-4x to the 3.5x-3.75x longer-term target through 2029.

While fixed reservation payments expire after 2029, the analyst expects the existing payout to remain covered via retained free cash flow, modest D-J growth, and potential operating efficiencies.

"All in, risk is overstated and growth upside is feasible (though not necessary)," Weston wrote.

data.title: OpenAI says it will train frontier models models in closed system with no internet access
data.description:
OpenAI (OPENAI) said on Friday that it is going to train its frontier artificial intelligence in a more secure environment, putting them in a closed system with no internet access.

“Working closely with cloud providers, we’ve added new controls throughout our infrastructure, reduced the attack surface that agents can exploit, and improved our methods for detecting misaligned behavior and attempts to cross security boundaries,” OpenAI said in a statement. “These protections overlap, so that containment can hold even if an individual control fails—a strategy known as defense in depth.”

The changes come after the Hugging Face incident in July as well as other instances in which AI models acted in ways other than intended. 

Led by CEO Sam Altman, OpenAI added that the investments have allowed the company to detect and stop misaligned behavior before damage was caused. The company cited an example on Sept. 20 in which an internal research model exploited a misconfiguration in a DNS resolver to gain limited access. The incident was contained, and the weakness indicated that further work was needed.

Nonetheless, OpenAI added that “increasingly capable models can find vulnerabilities or misconfigurations in even the most secure systems,” and it's up to companies like OpenAI, Anthropic (ANTHRO), and others to fix them. 

“These red-teaming experiments discovered previously unknown software vulnerabilities, as well as misconfigurations in our research infrastructure. We’ve remediated weaknesses our red-teaming agents discovered and—where these issues were present in open-source software—have worked with the relevant maintainers, under our Patch the Planet initiative, to disclose and fix them,” OpenAI explained.

The company continued: “As our red-teaming experiments continued, the number of vulnerabilities and misconfigurations that our agents identified declined significantly. While we view this as an encouraging signal about the strength of our infrastructure, we expect that future models will be able to identify and exploit vulnerabilities of which we’re not yet aware. We therefore view continuous red-teaming as a core part of our long-term strategy for strengthening the security of our research environments.”

Reinforcement learning training and internal inference of OpenAI's frontier models resumed on Oct. 1.

data.title: S&P 500 eyes third straight quarter of 25%+ earnings growth
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SP500) is on track for another period of robust profit expansion in the third quarter of 2026, even as higher oil and gas prices raise cost pressures across the economy.

FactSet data show the index’s blended year-over-year earnings growth rate at 29.5%. If that figure holds once all companies report, it would mark the third consecutive quarter of earnings growth above 25% for the benchmark.

Profitability remains exceptionally strong. The blended net profit margin for the S&P 500 stands at 14.9%. Should this rate become the final result, it would represent the second-highest net profit margin recorded since FactSet began tracking the metric in 2009.

Reporting is still early, with only 24% of S&P 500 companies having released results so far. Among those that have reported, 83% delivered earnings per share above analysts’ estimates, while 66% posted positive revenue surprises.

The combination of elevated growth and resilient margins suggests large-cap companies continue to convert sales into profits at a high rate despite commodity-price headwinds. As more results arrive in the coming weeks, investors will watch whether the current blended figures hold or shift as the remaining three-quarters of the index reports.

S&P 500 Funds: (SPY), (VOO), (IVV), (RSP), (SSO), (UPRO), (SH), (SDS), (SPXU), (FXAIX), (VFIAX), (VFFSX), and (SWPPX).

data.title: Genmab rises, Corcept falls on late-stage antibody-conjugate data for ovarian cancer
data.description:
• Genmab (GMAB) is up ~10% in Friday trading after reporting that a phase 3 trial of its antibody-drug conjugate, rinatabart sesutecan (Rina-S), met its primary goal for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer.
  • In the intent-to-treat population, Rina-S, a folate receptor alpha (FRα)-targeted, topoisomerase I (TOPO1)-inhibitor ADC, led to a 71% reduction in the risk of disease progression or death compared to investigator's choice of chemotherapy. In the primary analysis set group, the figure was 67%.
  • A secondary endpoint, overall survival, was also met in both populations. 
  • No new safety concerns were found in the RAINFOL-02 trial.
  • Corcept Therapeutics (CORT), which markets Lifyorli (relacorilant) for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer, is down ~21% on the news.

data.title: Anthropic unifies Claude Chat and Cowork for enterprise plans
data.description:
Anthropic (ANTHRO) has unified Claude Chat and Cowork for enterprise plan subscribers that can be used on web, desktop and mobile devices.

"The new unified Claude experience brings chat and Cowork together on web, desktop, and mobile," Anthropic posted today on its Claude Support webpage. "Members no longer choose between chat and Cowork before they start. Every conversation starts as a chat, and when a task needs to run code or work with files, Claude continues the same conversation in an isolated cloud sandbox managed by Anthropic, then returns the finished work for review."

The new unified experience was made generally available today but currently requires an administrator to turn it on. Anthropic said the unified experience will be turned on by default beginning Nov. 16.
